results.title: -O0 at production volume [mem]
results.what: Same comparison as the small-N flag tests, but the memory unit (outlier removal + summaries) processes N=1,000,000 samples (data-dominated regime).
results.testing: Once data dominate the footprint, does '-O0' still matter?
results.meaning: '-O0' raises image text+data+bss by 4,016 B (3.9%) versus '-O2 (baseline)'. Resident memory on Linux did not move measurably because demand paging only charges pages that are touched and RSS is counted in whole pages. Compiler flags act on code (tens of KB); at this N the heap holds tens of MB, so even a real code-size change is a rounding error in resident memory. At N=1,000,000 the baseline needs 31.5 MB resident, so the change is 0.0% of what the Critter must provision. On an MMU-less microcontroller the image change (+4,016 B (+3.9%)) is paid in full in flash/RAM, which Linux demand paging hides. Run time changed +62% (0.320 s -> 0.520 s): a memory/time trade-off to weigh, not ignore. Hypothesis (NEUTRAL) refuted: worth a closer look in the report (check the image breakdown in builds.log and the phase snapshots in phases.csv).

Static linking removes a FIXED cost (shared libc mapping, loader, relocations), so it saves about the same absolute amount at any N -- a shrinking percentage as data grow. At N=1,000,000 the baseline needs 24.0 MB resident, so the change is 2.2% of what the Critter must provision. On an MMU-less microcontroller the image change (+561.3 KB (+2709.9%)) is paid in full in flash/RAM, which Linux demand paging hides. Trade-off: image text+data+bss INCREASES (+561.3 KB (+2709.9%)).

results.title: -O0 at production volume [compute]
results.what: Same comparison as the small-N flag tests, but the compute unit (HVAC prediction) processes N=1,000,000 samples (data-dominated regime).
results.testing: Once data dominate the footprint, does '-O0' still matter?
results.meaning: '-O0' raises image text+data+bss by 4,084 B (6.4%) versus '-O2 (baseline)'. Resident memory on Linux did not move measurably because demand paging only charges pages that are touched and RSS is counted in whole pages. Compiler flags act on code (tens of KB); at this N the heap holds tens of MB, so even a real code-size change is a rounding error in resident memory. At N=1,000,000 the baseline needs 138.5 MB resident, so the change is 0.0% of what the Critter must provision. On an MMU-less microcontroller the image change (+4,084 B (+6.4%)) is paid in full in flash/RAM, which Linux demand paging hides. Run time changed +43% (0.420 s -> 0.600 s): a memory/time trade-off to weigh, not ignore. Hypothesis (NEUTRAL) refuted: worth a closer look in the report (check the image breakdown in builds.log and the phase snapshots in phases.csv).

conclusion: The largest single impact was F-LARGE-05 (-static at production volume [mem]): -656 KB (-2.0%) in max RSS. Shipping-relevant compiler/linker flags moved max RSS by at most 0 KB (-fconserve-stack) at small N. At production volume the biggest flag effect was 656 KB (2.0%). Flags shape the image and the stack; data structures and buffer lifetimes decide resident memory.
